page: Amazon Web Services c6a.metal is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors. It features 192 vCPUs across 96 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The architecture is x86_64. The server is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but features a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c6a.metal in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 289,127.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 117,677.53. It also demonstrates top-tier performance in cryptographic tasks, software compilation with Clang, and Redis SET operations, which reached 184.73 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 12,088.33 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the top 25% tier.

Because the server lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, it is not designed for local-storage-heavy databases or GPU-accelerated deep learning training. However, its high core density and strong memory bandwidth make it highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads. It is well-suited for high-performance computing, software compilation, batch processing, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM prompt processing.
